content.text:
I've removed the "Show more" button. The next batch of produce now loads by itself when the buyer scrolls near the end of the list.

**Why the button was showing:** the auto-load code was already written, but it never started working. It tried to attach to an invisible marker below the cards before the list had finished loading, when that marker didn't exist yet. Once loading finished, nothing made it try again. So the fallback button was always visible and buyers had to tap it.

**What I changed** (all in `src/app/consumer/page.tsx`):
- **Auto-load fixed:** the scroll watcher now waits until loading finishes, so it attaches properly.
- **Button removed:** a small green spinner shows under the cards while more are on the way. Loading still starts about 2 screens early, so on most phones the next cards are ready before the buyer reaches them.
- **Very old browsers:** if a browser can't watch scrolling, the page now shows all cards at once instead of showing a button.

TypeScript and the existing paging tests pass. I haven't added a new test, because this fix is about when the page component sets up the watcher, and the repo has no component tests for it. I also haven't opened it in a browser, so please scroll the `/consumer` page on staging (phone and desktop) to check it. Nothing is committed yet. Tell me when you want me to commit.

I found **22 places where buttons or menu items overlap**: 10 on the buyer side, 8 on the seller side and 4 in the moderator area. Removing the duplicates means about **20 fewer buttons and links**, plus **11 extra language toggles** in page headers. I haven't changed anything.

This is based on the current staging code, including your uncommitted changes. I read the code only; I didn't click through the app.

Most of the duplicates appeared because the **bottom menu bar** was added later and the older buttons were never removed. The general rule I'd suggest: **the bottom bar and the Settings page are the main way around, and anything that only repeats them goes.**

---

## Buyer side (`/consumer/...`)

| # | Item | Where it appears | Why it's redundant | Keep | Remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | **⚙️ menu at the top** | Top bar on the buyer home page (`GlobalNav.tsx`) | Every item in it also exists on the Settings page: My orders, My complaints, My address, Default dashboard, Log out, Switch role (Farmer / Aggregator / Delivery / Back to dashboard). Two "Settings" icons on one screen. Its "🛒 Shop as Consumer" item does nothing, because you're already in the shop. | Bottom bar **Settings** tab | The whole ⚙️ menu. Top bar keeps only the logo, language toggle and the **Login** button for logged-out users |
| B2 | **My orders** (3 places) | Bottom bar Orders tab (with red badge) · "🧾 My orders" chip on the home banner (`MyOrdersChip.tsx`, same badge) · ⚙️ menu | Same page, same badge count | Bottom bar **Orders** | Home banner chip (⚙️ item goes with B1) |
| B3 | **Order history** (2) | Settings → "Order history" row · Orders page → "History" tab | Same page. Buyers look for it on Orders, not Settings | Orders page **History** tab | Settings row |
| B4 | **Back to my dashboard** (seller shopping as a buyer: 4 places) | Bottom bar "My Store" tab · amber "Buyer view" strip at the top with a "↩ My farm" button · Settings row · ⚙️ menu | Four buttons doing the same thing | Bottom bar **My Store**, plus the amber strip's message (it explains the mode) | Strip's button, Settings row (⚙️ goes with B1) |
| B5 | **Language toggle EN/తె** (13 places) | Settings page, home top bar, and the headers of 11 more pages: orders, order history, order detail, farmers, profile, complaints, intents, produce, harvest, public farmer page, region page | People set the language once. 11 copies crowd every header at 390px | Settings page + home top bar | The 11 header copies |
| B6 | **"← Back" on main tab pages** | Orders, Farmers and Settings pages: each goes to `/consumer` | These pages are already bottom-bar tabs, and **Home** is one tap away on the same screen | Bottom bar **Home** | "← Back" on those 3 pages only. Keep it on sub-pages (order detail, history, profile, produce, harvest) |
| B7 | **My complaints** (3) | Settings row · ⚙️ menu · link at the bottom of the Orders page | ⚙️ copy is redundant. The Orders page link is useful there, where problems happen | Settings row + Orders page link | ⚙️ item (goes with B1) |
| B8 | **Crop requests / intents** (2) | Settings → "My crop requests" · home → "📋 My raised intents" next to Raise Intent | Small overlap; the home link makes sense next to the form | Both | Nothing. But it has 3 names ("intents", "demand", "crop requests"); pick one |
| B9 | **Floating cart button** (`CartFab`, used on 6 pages) | Home, produce, harvest, farmer page, region page, farmer tabs | Never shows. It hides itself wherever the bottom bar has the cart, which is now every buyer page. Code only, users never see it | Bottom bar **Cart** | The 6 `<CartFab />` uses (keep its "resume UPI payment" redirect by moving it elsewhere) |
| B10 | **Farmers list** (2) | Bottom bar Farmers (`/consumer/farmers`) · Region page "Farmers" tab | Both list farmers, but the region page is the public discovery page (P2) | Both | Nothing. Noted only |

**Related bug (not a duplicate):** "← Back" on **My complaints** and **My crop requests** goes to Home (`/consumer`). Buyers reach those pages from Settings, so it should go back to Settings.

---

## Seller side (farmer + aggregator dashboard, which share the same page)

| # | Item | Where it appears | Why it's redundant | Keep | Remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | **⚙️ Settings** (2) | Dashboard header link · bottom bar Settings tab | Both open the same Settings sheet | Bottom bar **Settings** | Header link |
| S2 | **Log out** (2) | Dashboard header link · inside the Settings sheet | Same action. A log-out link right in the header is easy to tap by mistake | Settings sheet | Header link |
| S3 | **Edit profile** (3) | Header "Edit profile" link · Settings sheet "Account" card · "Complete your profile → Fill details" card | The first two are the same; the third only shows when the profile is incomplete | Settings → **Account**, plus the "Complete profile" card | Header link |
| S4 | **Orders** (2 + shortcuts) | Bottom bar Orders tab · big "Orders – Open →" card on the dashboard | Same page with no filter | Bottom bar **Orders**, and the 3 stat cards (pending / today / approved), which open filtered views | Big "Orders" card |
| S5 | **Shop as buyer** (3) | Bottom bar "Shop as buyer" · "Buyer view" card → "🛒 Shop as buyer" · Settings → Switch role → "🛒 Shop as Consumer" | Same action, two different names | Bottom bar **Shop as buyer** | Card button + Settings item |
| S6 | **View my public page** (2) | Header "View profile ↗" · "Buyer view" card → "👁 Preview my shop" | Both open `/farmer/[slug]` | Header **View profile** | "Preview my shop". With S5, the whole "Buyer view" card (`BuyerViewSwitch`) can go |
| S7 | **"← Back" on the seller Orders page** | `/farmer/dashboard/orders` | It's a bottom-bar tab; Home is right there | Bottom bar **Home** | "← Back" |
| S8 | **Produce** (2) | Bottom bar Produce tab · "Active listings – Manage →" stat card | Same sheet, but the card shows the count | Both | Nothing |

**Note:** the seller Settings sheet has **no language option**. If you remove any seller header toggle, move it into the sheet first.

## Moderator area

| # | Item | Where | Why | Keep | Remove |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **Delivery agents vs Delivery riders** | Two menu items | "Agents" uses an old `delivery_agents` table with no login and no link to orders. The code's own comment says approving someone there never controls who delivers. Riders is the real one | **Delivery riders** | "Delivery agents" menu item and page. **Check with the client first** |
| M2 | **"+ Onboard a farmer"** | Dashboard quick action → `/moderator/farmers/new` | That address only redirects to `/moderator/register-farmer`, which the Farmers page links to directly | `/moderator/register-farmer` | The old redirect page (repoint the button) |
| M3 | **Quick actions repeat stat cards** | Moderator dashboard | "Review listings" = Pending approvals card, "View escalations" = Open escalations card, "View reports" = Orders/GMV cards, all on the same screen | Stat cards | Those 3 quick-action buttons (optional: some people don't realise the cards can be tapped) |
| M4 | **Farmer onboarding vs My farmers** | Two farmer-list pages | "My farmers" is the same list showing only the farmers you registered | Farmer onboarding page with a "Registered by me" filter | Separate "My farmers" page (low priority) |

**Checked, not duplicates:** "Reports" (zone performance) and "Order reports" (per-farmer payouts) are different pages with confusing names. I'd rename one of them, not remove it.

---

## Suggested order

1. **Highest value, low risk:** B1 (⚙️ menu), B2, S1–S2–S3, S5–S6. This removes the most visible double buttons.
2. **Cleanup:** B3, B4, B6, S4, S7, the complaints/intents Back bug, B9 (unused cart code).
3. **Needs your or the client's call:** B5 (language toggles), M1 (agents), M3, M4.

content.text:
Every page except the starting pages now has the same Back button. It takes the user to the page they actually came from.

**How it works**
- **One shared button** (`src/components/BackButton.tsx`). It looks the same everywhere: "← Back" / "← వెనక్కు", with a larger tap area for phones.
- **It goes to the last page visited.** A small invisible tracker in the root layout (`NavHistoryTracker.tsx`, rules in `src/lib/backNav.ts`) remembers the pages visited in the app in that tab. If there is one of our pages behind the current one, Back uses the browser's history, so it lands on the real previous page.
- **If there is no previous page, it goes to a sensible page.** This covers a page opened from a WhatsApp link, the home-screen icon or a new tab. Instead of leaving the app or doing nothing, Back goes to that page's natural parent. For example, a shared produce link goes to the shop home.

**Where it is now (24 pages and components)**
- **Buyer:** Settings, Orders, Order history, Order detail, Produce, Harvest, Farmers, Profile, Complaints, Crop requests, Buyer protection, Cart (its ← arrow), public farmer page, and the region page, which had no Back before.
- **Seller:** Orders, Order detail, Complaints, Aggregator farmers list.
- **Rider:** Complaints, Login, Signup.
- **Login and signup:** farmer and aggregator, all new. If there's no previous page, they go to `/home`.
- **Moderator:** every page except the moderator dashboard (added once in `ModeratorShell.tsx`).

When a farmer adds a new produce, the form already has an answer filled in for the "Delivery method" question, and that answer is **🧺 Pickup only** (your screenshot 1 showed this). The question is whether that pre-filled answer should be **🔁 Both** instead.

### Why it matters now
- Many farmers don't touch a box that is already filled in. They type the name and price and press Save.
- So their produce gets saved as **pickup-only**, even if they would happily deliver.
- Before today, nobody noticed, because the cart asked pickup/delivery on every item anyway.
- After today's change, pickup-only produce **stands out**: a "🚶 Pickup only" chip on the card, and an amber "pickup only" highlight in the cart when the buyer picks Home delivery.
- If most produce is pickup-only only because nobody changed the default, buyers will see these chips everywhere. Home delivery will look like it hardly works.

### Where "Pickup only" is the default today
1. The farmer's Add Produce form (`?? 'pickup'` in the farmer dashboard).
2. The moderator's Add Listing form.
3. The database column default (`DEFAULT 'pickup'`).

Produce that already exists is **not** affected by any change here. Only new produce gets the default.

### The three choices

| Option | What happens | Good | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Keep "Pickup only"** | No change | We never promise delivery a farmer can't do | Many items stay pickup-only by accident; home delivery looks weak |
| **B. Change to "Both"** | New produce allows pickup and delivery unless the farmer changes it | More items can be delivered; fewer chips | A farmer who can't deliver may get delivery orders without realising |
| **C. No default: the farmer must pick** | All three boxes start empty; Save asks the farmer to choose | Every farmer makes a real choice; no accidental pickup-only or accidental delivery | One extra tap when adding produce |

### My recommendation: C (make the farmer choose)
- It fixes the real problem, which is farmers not choosing at all. It doesn't swap one wrong guess for another.
- It is only one tap, once per produce.
- The moderator form would get the same rule, so the two stay in step (your farmer/moderator parity rule).

Before choosing B, one thing to check: the box says **"I will courier"**, which sounds like the **farmer** delivers. Home-delivery orders in the app are taken by **riders**. If riders do the delivery, "Both" is less risky and B also makes sense. If farmers really deliver themselves, C is the safer choice.

Tell me **A, B or C**. For B or C, I'll change the farmer form and the moderator form, add tests, and commit it separately. The database default can stay as it is, because both forms always send a value.

pagination means ?

**Pagination** means showing a long list **in parts (pages)** instead of all at once.

Example: you have 200 products. Instead of loading all 200 together (slow on 4G), you show:
- first 15,
- then the next 15,
- then the next 15, and so on.

### Two common styles

| Style | How the user gets the next part | Where you see it |
|---|---|---|
| **Page numbers** | Taps "1, 2, 3 … Next" | Google search results |
| **"Show more" button** | Taps a button at the bottom | Our app had this before today |
| **Infinite scroll** | Just keeps scrolling; the next part loads by itself | Instagram, Flipkart; **our app now** |

All three are kinds of pagination. Only the way the user asks for "the next part" is different.

### In our app (`/consumer` home page)
- The full produce list comes from the server in one go.
- The screen draws **15 cards at a time**.
- When the buyer scrolls near the bottom, the next 15 are drawn automatically. Earlier today this was the "Show more" button; now it's infinite scroll.
- **Why:** drawing 15 cards (and their photos) is much faster on a slow phone than drawing 200 at once.

So when someone says "add pagination", they mean "don't show everything at once, show it in parts".
